chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ayoub ibn al-Hurr, brother of Udaym, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
Whoever says ten times, 'O Lord, O Lord', it will be said to him, 'At your service! What is your need?'

key_terms.لَبَّيْكَ: At your service / I am responding to you
key_terms.يَا رَبِّ: O Lord (a form of addressing God emphasizing His lordship)

ai.seo_question: What is the reward for saying 'Ya Rabb' ten times?
ai.summary: Recorded in al-Kafi, this hadith highlights the efficacy of repetitive invocation (dhikr) as a means to attain immediate divine responsiveness, a concept central to Shia devotional practice. The direct response 'At your service' (Labbayk) underscores God's readiness to accept the plea, linking the act of calling upon the Lord with the fulfillment of specific worldly or spiritual needs.
